```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(circlize)
library(uwot)
```

<!-- -->

1.  **Downloaded data**

```{r}
# Explanation: I want to load the count data. I also want to generate some
# initial variables that I expect to use across code blocks.

tcga_data <- read.csv(file = "counts.csv", row.names = 1) # Read data from 
#"counts" CSV

# Check for any NAs in counts
sum(is.na(tcga_data))

esr1_gene <- tcga_data["ENSG00000091831",] # Instantiate expression values 
# for my gene of choice

esr1_numeric <- as.numeric(esr1_gene) # Instantiate numeric vector of 
# expression values for use throughout interpretations, as needed

erbb2_gene <- tcga_data["ENSG00000141736",] # Instantiate expression 
#values for my other gene of choice

erbb2_numeric <- as.numeric(erbb2_gene) # " " re: expression values
```

2)  **Summary Statistics**

```{r}
# Explanation: I want to generate summary statistics in a tidy way

summary_stats <- tibble(expression = esr1_numeric) %>% # Create data frame 
  # of numeric vector
  summarize( # Generate summary statistics with summarize() function
    mean = mean(expression, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(expression, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(expression, na.rm = TRUE),
    min = min(expression, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(expression, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

summary_stats # Return the statistical data

# Create a summary stats table
knitr::kable(
  summary_stats,
  caption = "Summary statistics for ESR1 expression."
)
```

3)  **Visualization**

<!-- -->

```{r}
# Explanation: I want a function to create the histogram, scatter,
# and violin plots. Since each plot function has a lot of similar
# data, and we're only working in this file, we can create a 
# function that generates all 3 plots.

library(ggpubr) # Since not part of the tidyverse, and we need ggarrange() below

create_plots <- function(first_gene_expression,
                         first_gene_name,
                         second_gene_name,
                         second_gene_numeric,
                         metadata,
                         fill_or_color = "#1B9E77") {
  
  # Because we want to make a new vector from the argument passed
  first_gene_numeric <- as.numeric(first_gene_expression)
  
  # Histogram
  hist_plot <- ggplot(
    data.frame(expression = first_gene_numeric),
    aes (x = expression)
  ) +
    
    geom_histogram(bins = 30,
                 alpha = 0.8,
                 fill = fill_or_color,
                 color = "black") +
    labs(
      title = paste("Distribution of", first_gene_name, "Expression"),
      x = "Gene expression value",
      y = "Frequency"
      ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(plot.margin = margin(15, 15, 15, 15), # I want the plot to have 
          # padding, including above title
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold",
                                    size = 12,
                                    margin = margin(t = 20, b = 10)),
          axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
          axis.text = element_text(size = 8)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 300000, by = 50000))
  
  
  # Scatter plot
  scatter_df <- data.frame(
    Gene_1 = first_gene_numeric,
    Gene_2 = second_gene_numeric
  )
  
  scatter_plot <- ggplot(
    scatter_df,
    aes(x = Gene_1, y = Gene_2)
  ) +
    geom_point( # Apply scatter geometry
    color = fill_or_color,
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
    
    # Add a regression line to the scatter plot
    geom_smooth(
      method = "lm",
      se = FALSE,
      color = "red",
      linewidth = 1) +
    
    # Add correlation annotation to show significance (bottom right)
    # I learned this method from Microsoft Copilot
    stat_cor(
      label.x.npc = 0.25,
      label.y.npc = 0.10,
      size = 3,
      color = "red") +
  
  # Since the expression ranges are so large, I want to log them in order 
  # to visualize/interpret the data more efficiently
  scale_x_log10(
    breaks = c(10, 100, 1000, 10000, 100000),
    labels = c("10", "100", "1,000", "10,000", "100,000")
  ) +
  scale_y_log10(
    breaks = c(1000, 10000, 100000, 1000000),
    labels = c("1,000", "10,000", "100,000", "1,000,000")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = paste(first_gene_name, "vs", second_gene_name, "Expression"),
    x = paste(first_gene_name, "Expression (log10)"),
    y = paste(second_gene_name, "Expression\n(log10)")
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold",
                                  size = 12,
                                  margin = margin(t = 20, b = 10)),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 8))
  
  
  # Violin Plot
  violin_data_frame <- tibble(
    
    # head(names(esr1_gene)) returns samples with a period separator. In 
    # order to match the metadata barcodes, we have to turn each period 
    # into a hyphen
    barcode = gsub("\\.", "-", names(first_gene_expression)),
    expression = first_gene_numeric
    ) %>%
    inner_join(
      metadata %>%
      select(barcode, ajcc_pathologic_stage),
      by = "barcode"
      ) %>%
    
    # The data have some NAs and X's in the ajcc_pathologic_stage column, 
    # which we want to filter out
    filter(!is.na(ajcc_pathologic_stage),
           ajcc_pathologic_stage != "Stage X")
  
  violin_plot <- ggplot(violin_data_frame,
                      aes(x = ajcc_pathologic_stage,
                          y = expression)) +
    geom_violin(fill = fill_or_color,
                alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_boxplot( # Add boxplots to visualize distribution of data,
      # with outliers colored red
      width = 0.1,
      fill = "white",
      outlier.size = 0.5,
      outlier.color = "red") +
    scale_y_log10(
      breaks = c(10, 100, 1000, 10000, 100000),
      labels = c("10", "100", "1,000", "10,000", "100,000")
      ) +
    labs(title = paste(first_gene_name, "Expression by Pathologic Stage"),
         x = "Pathologic Stage",
         y = paste(first_gene_name, "Expression\n(log10)")) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(
        angle = 45,
        hjust = 1,
        size = 8),
      plot.margin = margin(15, 15, 15, 15),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold",
                                size = 12,
                                margin = margin(t = 20, b = 10)),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 8))
  
  # Arrange plots
  all_plots <- ggarrange(ggarrange(hist_plot, scatter_plot,
                                   ncol = 2,
                                   labels = c("A", "B")),
                         violin_plot,
                         nrow = 2,
                         heights = c(1, 1.5), # Make violin plot larger
                         labels = c("", "C"))
  
  return(all_plots)
}
```

Create histogram, scatter, and violin plots...

```{r}
# Explanation: Now, I need to call the function with the data for each plot to
# generate the final plots. Thereafter, I save the plots to a PNG.

# I need to fetch the metadata to generate the violin plot
tcga_meta_data <- read.csv(file = "meta_data.csv")

final_plots <- create_plots(
  first_gene_expression = esr1_gene,
  first_gene_name = "ESR1",
  second_gene_name = "ERBB2",
  second_gene_numeric = erbb2_numeric,
  metadata = tcga_meta_data
)

final_plots

ggsave(
  filename = "SalaamRasheeda-Final Project Check-In Plots.png",
  plot = final_plots,
  width = 12,
  height = 8,
  dpi = 300
)
```

3D. **Heatmap Analysis**

```{r}
# Explanation: We have over 1,000 samples, so the heatmap will look busy. 
# I've done my best to allow for some readbility by structuring 
# the covariate colors to separate into broader pathologic stages.

# Select 10 consecutive genes, starting from ENSG00000091831-- my chosen 
# ESR1 gene
which(rownames(tcga_data) == "ENSG00000091831.24")
ten_genes <- rownames(tcga_data)[1944:1953]

# Filter covariate data to exclude NAs and X's
filtered_tcga_meta_data <- tcga_meta_data %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(ajcc_pathologic_stage),
    ajcc_pathologic_stage != "Stage X"
  )

# In counts data, replace period delimiter with hyphens
count_barcodes <- gsub("\\.", "-", colnames(tcga_data))

# Grab matching rows from filtered data to create subset below
samples_to_keep <- filtered_tcga_meta_data$barcode

# Subset these 10 genes into a data frame
tcga_data_subset <- tcga_data[
  ten_genes,
  count_barcodes %in% samples_to_keep
  ]

# Convert Ensemble IDs to common gene names
# for readability in heatmap
common_names <- c(
  "ENSG00000091831.24" = "ESR1",
  "ENSG00000091844.8" = "RGS17",
  "ENSG00000091879.14" = "ANGPT2",
  "ENSG00000091947.10" = "TMEM101",
  "ENSG00000091972.18" = "CD200",
  "ENSG00000091986.16" = "CCDC80",
  "ENSG00000092009.10" = "CMA1",
  "ENSG00000092010.15" = "PSME1",
  "ENSG00000092020.10" = "PPP2R3C",
  "ENSG00000092036.18" = "HAUS4"
)
rownames(tcga_data_subset) <- common_names[rownames(tcga_data_subset)]

# Get log of expression values for better readability for Heatmap() below
log_counts <- log10(tcga_data_subset + 1)

# Create heatmap annotations
ha_column <- HeatmapAnnotation(
  Pathologic_Stage = filtered_tcga_meta_data$ajcc_pathologic_stage,
  col = list(
    # Create a color palette that helps to visualize the broader stages, 
    # since we have so many samples
    Pathologic_Stage = c(
      "Stage 0" = "#000000",
      
      "Stage I" = "#66C2A5",
      "Stage IA" = "#41AE76",
      "Stage IB" = "#238B45",
      
      "Stage II" = "#8DA0CB",
      "Stage IIA" = "#4F81BD",
      "Stage IIB" = "#225EA8",
      
      "Stage IIIA"= "#FC8D62",
      "Stage IIIB"= "#F16913",
      "Stage IIIC"= "#D94801",
      
      "Stage IV" = "#E7298A"
      )
    )
  )

# Save heatmap to PNG with adequate dimensions
png(
"SalaamRasheeda-Final Project Check-in Heatmap.png",
width = 16000,
height = 8000,
res = 1200
)

# Generate heatmap
Heatmap(
  as.matrix(log_counts), # Because Heatmap() expects data in a matrix
  name = "Counts",
  top_annotation = ha_column,
  show_row_names = TRUE,
  row_names_gp = gpar(
    fontsize = 12,
    fontface = "bold"), # I want the common gene names emboldened
  show_column_names = FALSE, # We have 1,000+ samples, so showing the 
  # names would be very messy
  cluster_columns = TRUE,
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  column_title = "Samples",
  row_title = "Genes",
  heatmap_legend_param = list(title = "Count")
)

dev.off()
```

**FINAL SUBMISSION ADDITION: UMAP Plot (ie, new plot type)**

```{r}
# Explanation: For the final project, I want to generate a UMAP to see
# whether samples with similar ESR1 expression also show similar
# overall gene-expression patterns.

# Identify samples that exist in the filtered metadata
matched_samples <- count_barcodes %in%
filtered_tcga_meta_data$barcode

# Confirm that metadata and expression samples are in the same order
all(
  count_barcodes[matched_samples] ==
    filtered_tcga_meta_data$barcode
)

# Keep only samples with valid stage information
tcga_data_filtered <- tcga_data[, matched_samples]

# Log-transform expression values
tcga_data_log <- log10(tcga_data_filtered + 1)

# Calculate variance for each gene
gene_var <- apply(tcga_data_log, 1, var)

# Keep the 2,000 most variable genes
top_genes <- names(
  sort(gene_var, decreasing = TRUE)[1:2000]
)

# Subset data to the most variable genes
tcga_top <- tcga_data_log[top_genes, ]

# Transpose so rows = samples and columns = genes
expr_matrix <- t(as.matrix(tcga_top))

# Run PCA
pca_res <- prcomp(
  expr_matrix,
  center = TRUE,
  scale. = TRUE
)

# Set seed for reproducibility since UMAP
# coordinates can change at each run
set.seed(131)

# Run UMAP
umap_res <- umap(
  pca_res$x[, 1:50],
  n_neighbors = 15,
  min_dist = 0.3
)

# Create data frame containing UMAP coordinates
umap_df <- data.frame(
  UMAP1 = umap_res[, 1],
  UMAP2 = umap_res[, 2]
)

# Add ESR1 expression values for the samples included in the UMAP
# Log transform, as with heatmap
umap_df$ESR1 <- log10(esr1_numeric[matched_samples] + 1)

# Create ESR1 UMAP
esr1_umap <- ggplot(
  umap_df,
  aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, color = ESR1)
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(
    title = "UMAP Colored by ESR1 Expression",
    x = "UMAP 1",
    y = "UMAP 2",
    color = "ESR1 Expression\n(log10-transformed)"
    ) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold",
                                  hjust = 0.5))

# Save plot
ggsave(
  filename = "SalaamRasheeda-FinalProject-ESR1_UMAP.png",
  plot = esr1_umap,
  width = 10,
  height = 7,
  dpi = 300
  )
```

**FINAL SUBMISSION ADDITION: Summary statistics (ajcc_pathologic_stage and age_at_diagnosis)**

```{r}
# Explanation: For the final project, I also want to generate 
# summary statistics for my pahtologic stage covariate, and 
# for age at diagnosis

# Pathologic stage is a categorical variable
# so we can get counts and percentages for each stage, instead...
path_stage_summary_stats <- filtered_tcga_meta_data %>%
  count(ajcc_pathologic_stage) %>%
  mutate(
    Percent = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)
  )

path_stage_summary_stats

# Create a table
knitr::kable(
path_stage_summary_stats,
caption = "Distribution of samples by pathologic stage."
)

# Aside from filtering for NAs below, check for any unexpected age
# values that we'd want to filter out
unique(tcga_meta_data$age_at_diagnosis)

# Convert ages from days to years
years_old <- tcga_meta_data$age_at_diagnosis/365.25

age_summary_stats <- data.frame(
  mean = mean(years_old, na.rm = TRUE),
  median = median(years_old, na.rm = TRUE),
  sd = sd(years_old, na.rm = TRUE),
  min = min(years_old, na.rm = TRUE),
  max = max(years_old, na.rm = TRUE)
)

# Round the final values for relevance
round(age_summary_stats, 1)

# Create table
knitr::kable(
  round(age_summary_stats, 1),
  caption = "Summary statistics for age at diagnosis."
)
```
